punchline: You can be honest and talented and still not be trusted if people doubt your motives or your delivery.
thirty_sec: Stephen M. R. Covey breaks trust into four cores of credibility: integrity, intent, capabilities and results. The first two are character, the last two competence. He compares them to the four ways a lawyer can discredit an expert witness: attack their honesty, their motives, their qualifications or their record. Lose any one core and trust wobbles, but naming which one is missing makes the problem fixable.
question: If someone doubted you at work, which of the four cores would they question first?
